_why: Chips that no vocabulary term names, on a lab whose own package.json depends on something of that name. Each row is a DECLARED decision that the chip is not an algorithm this index can carry, with the reason. The denominator is declared here rather than discovered by the checker, because a chip that quietly stops being flagged is the same silence the checker exists to end. Removing a row makes catalog-sync.js vocab fail until a term exists or the row comes back.

exempt.why: KpqC is Korea's post-quantum standardisation PROGRAMME, not an algorithm. The algorithms it selected — SMAUG-T, HAETAE, AIMer, NTRU+ — are the indexable things, and the first two already have terms. A term named for the competition would credit a lab with implementing a committee.
A category, and the package is a library of many algorithms rather than one. The chip says which shelf this lab is on; ML-DSA is what it implements, and that already has a term and an anchor.

A certificate FORMAT, not an algorithm. The algorithms inside a certificate — RSA, ECDSA, SHA-256 — are indexed separately and are what the reverse index is asked about. Indexing the container would put every PKI lab under a term that answers no question about which primitive it builds.

The same decision already recorded for crypto-lab-chain-of-trust, applied to the second lab that parses certificates with the same package: X.509 is a certificate FORMAT, not an algorithm. What this lab actually computes inside that format -- ECDSA over P-256 and P-384 signature verification in WebCrypto -- is indexable on its own terms, and indexing the container would put a PKI lab under a term that answers no question about which primitive it builds.
